egyptianMarble.pageTitle: Egyptian Marble – Slabs, Tiles & Blocks from Egypt | Wadi Degla
egyptianMarble.metaDescription: Egyptian marble from Wadi Degla: Galala, Sunny, Triesta, Fantazia, Emperador, Cleopatra and more. Slabs, tiles and blocks from our own quarries and factories in Egypt, exported worldwide since 1980.
egyptianMarble.heading: Egyptian Marble
egyptianMarble.intro:
Egyptian marble is natural stone quarried in Egypt, known for its warm beige, cream, grey and brown tones and its consistent quality. It is used in homes, hotels, resorts and commercial buildings around the world.

Wadi Degla has worked Egyptian quarries since 1980, when our founder opened the first quarry on Galala Mountain. Today we cut and finish Egyptian marble in our own factories in Egypt, covering more than 27,000 square meters, and ship it as slabs, tiles and blocks to projects worldwide. Below you will find every Egyptian marble we supply, followed by answers to the questions buyers ask most.

sections.title: Popular types of Egyptian marble
sections.text:
Our Egyptian range includes Galala and Galala Extra, Sunny Light and Sunny Dark, Triesta Beige and Triesta Grey, Fantazia Sylvia and Fantazia Sunny, Melly Grey, Emperador, Cleopatra, Imperial, Katrina, Creamy White Pearl and Egyptian alabaster.

Each stone has its own page with its photos, available finishes and the projects where it was used.

sections.title: Where Egyptian marble is used
sections.text: Flooring, wall cladding, facades, staircases, window sills, countertops and landscaping, in villas, hotels, resorts, residential compounds and commercial buildings. Our projects with Egyptian marble include resorts in the Caribbean, residential buildings in Kenya, villas and business buildings in Egypt and an embassy in Kuwait.

sections.title: Finishes and formats
sections.text: Depending on the stone, Egyptian marble is available polished, honed, brushed, antique, sandblasted, bush hammered, flamed, leather and split face. We supply blocks, slabs and cut-to-size tiles, and our factories can produce custom dimensions for your project.

sections.title: Why buy Egyptian marble from Wadi Degla
sections.text: Three generations in Egypt's quarrying industry, quarries on Galala Mountain, and three factories (opened in 2000, 2011 and 2015) with modern sawing, polishing, resin, CNC and waterjet lines. Our production is ISO certified, every order is packed in export-grade wooden bundles, crates or pallets, and we ship to the GCC, Europe, Africa, Asia and the Americas.

faq.q: Is Egyptian marble good for flooring?
faq.a: Yes. Egyptian marbles such as Galala, Sunny and Triesta are widely used for indoor flooring in homes, hotels and commercial buildings. For outdoor or wet areas, a honed, brushed or sandblasted finish gives better grip than a polished one.

faq.q: What is the difference between Egyptian and imported marble?
faq.a: Egyptian marble is quarried and processed in Egypt. Imported marbles, from partner quarries in Italy, Turkey and other countries, add colours and veining that Egyptian quarries don't produce, such as pure whites with bold veins. Wadi Degla supplies both, so you can source a whole project from one supplier.

faq.q: Can I get a sample?
faq.a: Yes. Open any stone's page and press "Request a sample", or contact our sales team.

faq.q: Do you export Egyptian marble?
faq.a: Yes. We export slabs, tiles and blocks with protective packing and full export documentation to the GCC, Europe, Africa, Asia and the Americas.

faq.q: How do I get a price?
faq.a: Prices depend on the stone, finish, thickness, sizes, quantity and destination. Send us your requirements and our sales team will reply with a quotation.

egyptianGranite.pageTitle: Egyptian Granite – Slabs, Tiles, Kerbstones & Cobbles | Wadi Degla
egyptianGranite.metaDescription: Egyptian granite from Wadi Degla: Black Aswan, Red Aswan, New Halayeb, Gandolla, Royal Red, Rosa El Nasr and more. Slabs, tiles, blocks, kerbstones and cobbles, exported worldwide.
egyptianGranite.heading: Egyptian Granite
egyptianGranite.intro:
Egyptian granite is hard, dense natural stone quarried in Egypt, in black, red, pink, grey, white and green tones. Because it resists wear and weather, it is chosen for busy floors, stairs, facades, kitchen countertops, kerbstones and outdoor paving.

Wadi Degla supplies Egyptian granite as slabs, tiles and blocks, and produces granite kerbstones and cobbles, all cut and finished in our own factories in Egypt.

sections.title: Popular types of Egyptian granite
sections.text: Our Egyptian granites include Black Aswan, Red Aswan, New Halayeb and Halayeb, Gandolla, Royal Red, Rosa El Nasr, Rosa Hoody, Red Fersan, Karnak Grey, Fantastic White, Verdi Green, Brown Qusair, Hoody Dark and Magic Noir.

sections.title: Where Egyptian granite is used
sections.text: Floors in airports, malls, offices and hotels; stairs and steps; exterior cladding and facades; kitchen countertops; and kerbstones, cobbles and paving for roads, walkways and landscapes.

sections.title: Finishes
sections.text: Polished for a deep shine indoors; flamed, bush hammered and sandblasted for slip-resistant outdoor surfaces; honed and leather for a soft matte look. The finishes available for each granite are shown on its page.

sections.title: Granite kerbstones and cobbles
sections.text: Besides slabs and tiles, our factories produce granite kerbstones in several profiles, and granite cobbles for driveways, walkways and squares, in standard and custom sizes.

faq.q: Is granite harder than marble?
faq.a: Yes. Granite is harder and less porous than marble, which is why it is preferred for heavy traffic, outdoor use and kitchen countertops.

faq.q: Which finish is best for outdoor granite?
faq.a: A flamed, bush hammered or sandblasted finish. The textured surface is slip resistant, which matters for paving, steps and areas around pools. Our team can recommend a stone and finish for your climate and use.

faq.a: Yes. Open any stone's page and press "Request a sample", or contact our sales team.

faq.q: How do I get a price?
faq.a: Prices depend on the stone, finish, thickness, sizes, quantity and destination. Send us your requirements and our sales team will reply with a quotation.

importedMarble.pageTitle: Imported Marble – Italian, Turkish & Exotic Marble | Wadi Degla
importedMarble.metaDescription: Imported marble from Wadi Degla: Calacatta, Arabescato, Botticino, Volakas, Nero Marquina, onyx and more, alongside our Egyptian stone. Slabs and tiles for luxury projects worldwide.
importedMarble.heading: Imported Marble
importedMarble.intro:
Alongside Egyptian stone, Wadi Degla supplies imported marble through our partnerships with quarries in Italy, Turkey and other countries: classic whites such as Calacatta and Arabescato, elegant greys, dark marbles such as Nero Marquina, and decorative onyx and exotic stones.

This means you can source the Egyptian and imported stones for a project from one supplier.

sections.title: Imported marbles we supply
sections.text:
Whites and greys: Calacatta Italy, Calacatta Grey, Calacatta Viola, Arabescato, Volakas, Majestic White, Oriental White, Panda White, Sunny White, Pietra Grey, Tundra Grey, Silver Grey, Lady Grey, Persian Grey and Universal Grey.

Beiges and browns: Botticino Classico, Breccia Daino, Travertine Beige, Diana Royal, Coffee Wood, Forest Brown and White Wood.

Dark and colourful: Nero Marquina, Azul Macauba, Iron Red, Forest Green and Silver Wave.

Onyx and exotic stones: Beige Onyx, Green Onyx, Indian Onyx, Amethyst, Blue, Brown and Grey Agate, Jasper, Ocean Jasper, Tiger Eye, Yellow Quartz and Petrified Wood.

sections.title: Where imported marble is used
sections.text: Feature walls, luxury bathrooms, hotel lobbies, reception desks, kitchen islands, stairs and furniture. Backlit onyx and exotic stones create statement walls, bars and counters.

sections.title: Finishes and formats
sections.text: Imported marble is mostly supplied as polished or honed slabs and tiles. The finishes available for each stone are shown on its page.

faq.q: What is the difference between Calacatta and Carrara marble?
faq.a: Both are white Italian marbles. Calacatta usually has a brighter white background with bolder, thicker veining, while Carrara is greyer with finer, softer veining.

faq.q: Can I combine imported and Egyptian marble in one project?
faq.a: Yes. Many projects use an imported marble for feature areas and an Egyptian marble for large floor and wall areas. We supply both.

faq.a: Prices depend on the stone, finish, thickness, sizes, quantity and destination. Send us your requirements and our sales team will reply with a quotation.

Imported granite is hard and durable, which makes it a favourite for kitchen countertops, busy floors, stairs and facades.

sections.title: Where imported granite is used

faq.q: Is imported granite good for kitchen countertops?

galalaMarble.pageTitle: Galala Marble – Egyptian Beige Marble from the Galala Quarries | Wadi Degla
galalaMarble.metaDescription: Galala marble: Egypt's best-known beige marble, from the Galala Mountain quarries opened by Wadi Degla's founder in 1980. Slabs, tiles and blocks in many finishes, exported worldwide.
galalaMarble.heading: Galala Marble
galalaMarble.intro:
Galala marble is Egypt's best-known beige marble, quarried in the Galala Mountain. It is valued for its durability, refined texture, consistent colour and timeless beige tone, and is used in residential, commercial and large architectural projects around the world.

Wadi Degla's story is tied to Galala: our founder opened the first Galala quarry in 1980, at a time when the mountain's marble was unknown.

sections.title: The story of Galala
sections.text: In 1980, Wadi Degla's founder, Alhag Saed Alghanam, explored the then-unknown potential of the Galala Mountain and opened its first quarry. Galala soon became one of Egypt's most sought-after stones, attracting importers from around the world. Under his leadership, Wadi Degla went on to own seven major quarries in Galala, and the second generation developed seven more.

sections.title: Why architects choose Galala
sections.text: High structural strength and durability, consistent colour and stone quality, and a warm beige that suits both classic and modern designs. It is used for floors, walls, facades, staircases and window sills in villas, hotels, compounds and commercial buildings.

sections.title: Finishes and formats
sections.text: Galala is available in many finishes, including polished, honed, brushed, antique, sandblasted, bush hammered, flamed, leather, rough and split face. We supply it as blocks, slabs and cut-to-size tiles, packed for export.

faq.q: Is Galala marble or limestone?
faq.a: Geologically, Galala is a compact limestone. In the stone trade it is sold as marble because it takes a polish and is used in the same ways as marble.

faq.q: What is the difference between Galala and Galala Extra?
faq.a: Both come from the Galala quarries. Each has its own page with photos, so you can compare their colour and texture.

faq.q: Can I get a Galala sample?
faq.a: Yes. Open the stone's page and press "Request a sample", or contact our sales team.

faq.q: How do I get a price for Galala marble?
faq.a: Prices depend on the finish, thickness, sizes, quantity and destination. Send us your requirements and our sales team will reply with a quotation.

buyGuide.pageTitle: How to Buy Marble & Granite from Egypt – Export Guide | Wadi Degla
buyGuide.metaDescription: How to import marble and granite from Egypt with Wadi Degla: choosing stones and samples, quotations, production, export packing, shipping and documents. Exporting worldwide since 1980.
buyGuide.heading: How to Buy Marble from Egypt
buyGuide.intro: Egypt is one of the world's major sources of natural stone, and Wadi Degla has exported Egyptian marble and granite since 1980. This guide explains how ordering from us works, from choosing a stone to receiving your container.

steps.title: Choose your stones
steps.text: Browse our Egyptian marble, Egyptian granite and imported stones, try them on real rooms with the Material Visualizer, and request samples of the ones you like.

steps.title: Send us your requirements
steps.text: Tell us the stone, finish, thickness, sizes (slabs, cut-to-size tiles or blocks), quantity and destination port. If you have drawings or a project schedule, send them too.

steps.title: Receive a quotation
steps.text: Our sales team prepares a quotation for your order and answers any technical questions.

steps.title: Production and quality control
steps.text: Your order is cut and finished in our factories in Egypt, with quality checks on the stone and on the finished pieces.

steps.title: Export packing
steps.text: Slabs are grouped in bundles of 8 to 15 pieces in reinforced wooden frames, or loaded on wooden bars for manual loading. Tiles go into foam-lined wooden crates or onto strapped pallets. Polished surfaces are protected with plastic sheets, and every crate and pallet is labelled with sizes, thickness and order details.

steps.title: Shipping and documents
steps.text: Our export department coordinates container loading, freight forwarders and customs documentation, so your shipment clears customs in your country without delays.

sections.title: Where we export
sections.text: We ship natural stone to the GCC, Europe, Africa, Asia and North and South America, with professional logistics, secure packing and full export documentation.

faq.q: Do you supply both Egyptian and imported stone?
faq.a: Yes. Besides our Egyptian marble and granite, we supply imported marble and granite from partner quarries, so a whole project can be sourced from one supplier.

faq.q: Can you produce custom sizes?
faq.a: Yes. We supply standard sizes, and our factories can cut custom dimensions to your drawings.

faq.q: How are slabs protected during shipping?
faq.a: Slabs travel in reinforced wooden bundles or on wooden bars, with plastic sheets between polished faces, and are strapped so they don't shift at sea.

faq.q: How do I start?
faq.a: Contact our sales team with your stone, quantities and destination, or request a sample from any stone's page.
